course_title: Short Term Mine Planning and Scheduling
course_description:
This course integrates technical mining knowledge relating geology, equipment capabilities, dig and dump designs, customer specifications, environmental requirements with project management theory to deliver robust short-term mine plans. This course focuses on minimising deviation to the targets set out in the long-term strategic planning and scheduling process.

This course provides practical skills in short-term mine planning, focusing on data-driven decision-making, orebody knowledge, mine design, operational safety, and asset performance management. Participants will engage with and integrate mine planning tools, optimize resources, and improve execution efficiency.

course_contacts.name: Dr Micah Nehring
course_contacts.notes: Consultation will be during the fortnightly online check-ins. Other consultation can be arranged via email.

timetable:
Additional timetable information
This course runs as a flexible online offering across the first 7 weeks of the semester with all course content available from the outset. Fortnightly online check-ins with course participants will take place across this 7-week period. Students unable to make these online check-ins should endeavor to catch-up with the Course Coordinator at a alternative time. In addition to this, an on-campus in-person workshop is scheduled for Week 8. Participants will present the outcomes of their project at the on-campus workshop with submission of the final report due shortly after.
course_aims: This course aims to equip students to develop robust short/medium term mine plans that seek to execute on the targets set out in the strategic plan.

learning_outcomes.description: Assess the context in which they are to undertake an execution plan with consideration and compliance to technical, environmental and social variables.
Hypothesise, test, and validate a critical path to improve mining production.
Communicate the decision-making process in relevant mining contexts to empower operations and other stakeholders.
Develop and justify contingency plans to provide alternative paths to achieve the main objective of the mine execution plan.
Identify and use appropriate project management tools and strategies to develop and evaluate an execution plan.
Visualise the critical path of key production milestones to various stakeholders using appropriate software tools.
Apply appropriate mathematical techniques in the decision-making process to inform the critical path.
Reflect on mining project plans and industry practitioners to derive future consideration for professional practice.

learning_activities.topic: Module 1: Foundations of short-term planning and scheduling The first module of this course introduces the key components of the short-term planning and scheduling process and its role within the broader mine planning process and mining value chain. The objective of short-term scheduling, the time horizons involved, and general resource and sequencing constraints are discussed. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L08

Module 2: Gantt Charts Module 2 introduces Gantt Charts. Gantt Charts are a very common way of communicating plans and schedules - not just in mining but across a range of industries. This is followed by a section on Critical Paths. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07, L08

Module 3: Critical path This module introduces Network Diagrams and Critical Path Method (CPM). Strategies to potentially reduce completion times across a given schedule are addressed. Learning outcomes: L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07

Module 4: Introduction to mathematical optimisation The focus of this module is to further enhance a mine planner's decision-making capability by introducing mathematical optimisation concepts which often form the basis for many of the computerised planning tools that are commercially available. Learning outcomes: L02, L05, L06, L07

Module 5: Mathematical optimisation The focus of this module is on the developing Linear Programming (LP) and Mixed Integer Programming (MIP) models to aid in the solution of complex mining related scheduling problems. Learning outcomes: L02, L05, L06, L07

Module 6: Waste Management and Dumping Operations This module introduces Inventory Management practise and Lean Theory as it applies to short-term mine planning and scheduling. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04
Module 7: Geology This module assesses the role that the geology of both the ore and the host rock play in the development of a short term mine plan. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04
Module 8: Equipment Deployment This module details the important role of equipment deployment and its impact on bench design. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04
Module 9: Waste Dump Management This module focuses on the role that waste dumps and their design have on ensuring a sustainable post mine land use for the site. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04

Module 10: Dumping Operations This module focuses on the short-term planning and scheduling aspects unique to waste materials (overburden) and the fundamentals of waste dump operations. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04
Module 11: Compliance This module introduces operational compliance aspects as it applies to short-term mine planning and scheduling. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L08
Module 12: Reconciliation This module introduces operational reconciliation aspects as it applies to short-term mine planning and scheduling. Learning outcomes: L01, L03, L04, L07, L08
